note: Frequency from frequency.json (coded sample). Cost, buyer, gap and agent fit are judgments against rubric.md; gap uses competitors-a.md / competitors-b.md.

pains.label: AI-written code needs cleaning up
pains.cost_why: Hours to days of rework per change; first-hand: 'net negative', 'codebase becomes unmanageable'. Security pass rate of AI code 56% (Veracode 2026). Not 5: impact per occurrence varies.
pains.buyer_why: Existing budget line: teams pay $24-72/user for CodeRabbit, SonarQube, Qodo, Codacy.
pains.gap_why: (c) Detection is plentiful; nothing stops slop being produced or does the rework.
pains.fit_why: Multi-step (read change, find problems, rework, test), across repo/CI/PR, needs judgment, and a person approves before merge.

pains.label: Code review is overloaded
pains.cost_why: Multi-day delay shown in our own data: first approval takes 20-23h median, 37-70% of time to merge (G1); vendor data: review time up 441% with AI adoption.
pains.buyer_why: Existing budget line: CodeRabbit, Greptile, Graphite, Copilot review, Claude Code Review.
pains.gap_why: Bot first pass is near-commoditized (b), but the core, human reviewer throughput, is unaddressed and bots add comments to read. Scored between (b) and (d).
pains.fit_why: Triage, split, summarize, pre-verify and route: multi-step, multi-tool, judgment, and the human decision stays human.

pains.label: Supervising agents is hard
pains.cost_why: Hours of babysitting and decision fatigue; first-hand: 'constantly context-switching human-in-the-loop', agents ignoring feedback.
pains.buyer_why: Clear team owner; teams already pay for agents (Cursor $40, Devin), supervision spend plausible but not yet its own line.
pains.gap_why: (c) Many dashboards to start and watch agents; little to trust what an agent did unattended.
pains.fit_why: A verifying agent checking another agent's work is the native shape; checkable before merge.

pains.label: Tech debt never gets prioritised
pains.cost_why: A slow drag rather than an acute per-occurrence cost; first-hand: debt 'struggles for priority with regular work'.
pains.buyer_why: Engineering leadership buys CodeScene, Jellyfish, Sonar; prioritisation itself has no clear line.
pains.gap_why: (d) Measuring debt is commoditized; nothing turns it into a business case that wins roadmap trade-offs.
pains.fit_why: Mostly a prioritisation and culture problem; an agent could draft the case but the decision is organisational.

pains.label: Knowledge lives in people's heads
pains.cost_why: Days to rebuild lost context; first-hand: bus factor of 1 in 50, 'last person to work on X left 6 years ago'.
pains.buyer_why: Existing budget line: Glean, Confluence + Rovo, Notion, Guru.
pains.gap_why: (c) Search over existing docs is well served; capturing what's in heads and keeping it current isn't.
pains.fit_why: An agent can capture knowledge from PRs and threads and keep docs current; checkable, but quality of capture is the weak point.

pains.label: Interruptions and context switching
pains.cost_why: 10-45 minutes to recover per interruption (research); hours a day in aggregate, but each occurrence is small.
pains.buyer_why: A team problem without a clear owner; tools are cheap individual purchases ($10-22).
pains.gap_why: (d) Calendars are covered; ad-hoc pings and tool switching aren't; the leading team tool shut down.
pains.fit_why: Mostly needs norms and UI, not an agent; an agent can batch pings but the fix is cultural.

pains.label: Too many tools
pains.cost_why: Hours of duplicated work; first-hand: permissions in 2+ places, 'drowning in scattered tools'.
pains.buyer_why: IT and ops buy tools, but fixing fragmentation has no clear owner.
pains.gap_why: (d) Every fix is another tool (suites or sync layers); fitting tools to the team's process isn't addressed.
pains.fit_why: An agent can act across tools, but a simpler integration often does.

pains.label: Vague or changing requirements
pains.cost_why: Rework and failed estimates; first-hand: 'as soon as requirements change the abstractions fall apart'; research ties it to project failure.
pains.buyer_why: Product leaders buy Productboard, ChatPRD, Jira Product Discovery.
pains.gap_why: (d) Tools speed up writing specs; none track why requirements change or check shipped code against the spec.
pains.fit_why: An agent can check code against the spec and flag drift, but the core is human decisions.

pains.label: Nobody understands the code
pains.cost_why: Slow, risky debugging and review; Anthropic RCT: AI group ~50% vs 67% comprehension; first-hand: 'losing grip on what we were building'.
pains.buyer_why: Budget exists for code intelligence (Sourcegraph, Unblocked), not yet for comprehension itself.
pains.gap_why: (d) Tools explain code when asked; none makes sure a person understood a change before it merged.
pains.fit_why: An agent can walk a reviewer through a change and check understanding; the human side is the weak point.

pains.label: AI tools lack the team's context
pains.cost_why: Repeating conventions and fixing output; hours per week; first-hand: 'I have to remind the LLM we changed that later'.
pains.buyer_why: Teams pay for Augment, Sourcegraph, Unblocked.
pains.gap_why: (c) Loading context is easy; nothing reliably makes agents follow it.
pains.fit_why: Agent-native: checking output against team rules is multi-step, multi-tool and verifiable.

pains.label: Approvals and sign-offs stall work
pains.cost_why: Our data: changes reviewed by 2+ roles take 1.70x longer (G3), 2.6x for small changes; first-hand: blocked for months.
pains.buyer_why: Spans roles, so ownership is unclear; CODEOWNERS tooling is free.
pains.gap_why: (d), close to (e): tools route approvals between engineers; nothing coordinates design, security and product sign-off.
pains.fit_why: Route, summarize for each role, chase and track across tools; the sign-off itself stays human.

pains.label: Non-engineers depend on engineering
pains.cost_why: Small changes; at GitLab non-engineers' changes are approved faster (G2, 0.59x).
pains.buyer_why: Marketing and product teams pay for CMSs, Builder.io, LaunchDarkly.
pains.gap_why: (c) Copy is close to solved by CMSs; UI tweaks reach a PR but still wait on an engineer.
pains.fit_why: Agents can make the change and open the PR; review stays human.
